chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said:

There neither has been, nor will there be, nor is there any believer except that he has a neighbor who harms him; and if a believer were on an island from the islands of the sea, Allah would surely send to him someone who would harm him.

key_terms.الْبَحْرِ: the sea, used to stress extreme distance from people
key_terms.جَارٌ: a neighbor; here, someone in close social proximity
key_terms.جَزِيرَةٍ: an island, indicating isolation and remoteness
key_terms.مُؤْمِنٌ: a believer; here, one whose faith is accompanied by worldly trial
key_terms.يُؤْذِيهِ: harms him or causes him distress

ai.seo_question: Does every believer face harm from people around him?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that being tested through harm from others is a recurring condition in the life of the believer. It emphasizes the inevitability of social trial and points to the believer’s need for patience in enduring such affliction.
